# EXPLORATORY — crystal / unit-cell / copy-provenance checks

**EXPLORATORY throughout: post hoc, nothing registered.** Generated by `experiments/crystal_check.py` from the CSVs in this directory. Existing registered numbers are comparators, not registrations for this analysis.

## EXPLORATORY H1 — not addressable as a complete quantitative X1 explanation; local forecast contradicted

Differential encounters use the existing X1 default Algocell executor shaders from the checked-out base commit 4cdb503, 128 instructions, the serial panel definitions, X1's 32 seeded alternative values/site, and 16 uniform partners (arm U distribution). Mutant and control encounters share partners. The observational shader records every opcode/prefix fetch, operand/displacement fetch, non-fetch data read and write. All differential and wild-type final memories are checked against the uninstrumented executor; all mutant fetch masks also match the existing `exectrace` tooling. Roles are address roles during the offspring's own next encounter; self modification can change the value occupying an address. `probes_*` records every intervention, copy gate and mutant window; `provenance_*` records changed and verbatim edges and the corresponding address roles in their next execution; `roles_*` records every offspring position.

The forecast freezes the wild-type local map: an edge exists when >=half sampled values copy verbatim at a particular destination/context; compose that map, and require survival in >=half contexts. The strict forecast removes opcode destinations at each child generation; the transmission-only forecast does not. Neither includes X1's branching survival, 75% copy gate, five-byte window, background subtraction, cap or fresh context resampling. Neither is an invariant-family certificate. Those omissions are explicit mechanisms by which a local map can fail to predict X1.

A separate first-encounter diagnostic adds the 75% copy gate and five-byte window, conditioning on copy survivors and requiring >=half sampled values/site, with no background/branching correction. Its g1 site counts are genome20_s6003: 9, ldir32: 0, pusher16: 2, pusher64: 28, ret16: 0. Per-site disagreements with X1 are preserved in `site_prediction_comparison.csv`. This diagnostic explains why isolated byte equality is too permissive for genome20: positions 6–14 preserve their complete windows in every sampled encounter, whereas the displacement operands can match a byte without reproducing their mutant window or a viable lineage. It is still a different assay from X1.

Arm K is a registered comparison only: pusher64 32/14/0/0; no K-context map was measured. The U map cannot quantitatively explain K. Opcode-fetched and operand-fetched are distinct; the older `exectrace` annotation calls both “executed”. A verbatim differential response is local causal evidence, not proof that one source supplies the byte for every value and descendant. Changes to opcodes/addresses can produce nonlinear changed positions. Rare working core alleles are not ruled out by a zero thresholded site score.

## EXPLORATORY H2 — contradicted as a universal equality; restricted offset count supported

A cyclic period p is the smallest divisor of L whose prefix tiles the tape. Every finite tape has trivial cyclic period L; “periodic” without p<L is unfalsifiable. `finite_period` separately uses the finite-factor definition T[i]=T[i+p] without a divisibility requirement. Sources remain separate: repeated tapes, snapshots, generation endpoints and the alternative 6502 64-partner scoring are not independent replicates.

Offset table: 2347 rows; 2343 have 0<d<=L and d|L; 2342/2343 have n_unexec=d−4; 2289/2343 have total sites=d−4. These are scan scores, not all-value serial capacities. A core motif plus dividing d alone does not establish all Proposition 8 prerequisites.

- EXPLORATORY deficit: I, L=16, seed 4004, final: p=16, d=8, n_unexec=0, predicted=4; `c8 5e ed b0 e9 c2 ad 00 9a fd d3 f5 be 3e 31 cc`. Prefix tiling agrees at 8/16 original positions; the 75% viability gate can reject the projected offspring. This is a gate diagnosis, not proof of loss of eligible payload.
- EXPLORATORY extra total sites: 53 rows; all have predicted unexecuted counts: True. Their excess is executed-site transmission under the sampled scorer; per-site masks/alleles are absent from this table.
- EXPLORATORY excluded offset geometry: 4 rows; fully listed in `cell_exceptions.csv` (nondividing offsets or d>L).
- EXPLORATORY minimal-period counterexample: K, L=32, seed 5006, final, `c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0 c8 5e ed b0` has p=4, d=8, and 4 unexecuted scored sites. The minimal four-byte unit is entirely core, predicting zero under p−c, whereas the copying prefix has eight bytes and four free positions. Mutable capacity is set by the invariant copying family, not the minimal period of its unmutated member.
- EXPLORATORY targeted validation (copy gate deficit): four payload values/site, 16 partners, eight transfers. Minimum continuous verbatim fraction at g8=1.000; minimum continuous 75% copy-gate fraction=0.000. Offspring periods at g8: 8. Wild-type first-transfer similarity=0.500. Full interventions in `offset_examples.csv`.
- EXPLORATORY targeted validation (unit-cell expands under mutation): four payload values/site, 16 partners, eight transfers. Minimum continuous verbatim fraction at g8=1.000; minimum continuous 75% copy-gate fraction=1.000. Offspring periods at g8: 8. Wild-type first-transfer similarity=1.000. Full interventions in `offset_examples.csv`.

For generic population cells the tables provide fetched union e, not the fetched residue set. The admissible payload interval is [p−min(p,e), p−ceil(e/(L/p))]. With p=L this is exact; with smaller p it is a bound. Serial tables have explicit fetched bitmaps, which are collapsed into unit-cell residues exactly. “Equal” is compatibility of sampled unexecuted counts with a fetched-only model, not evidence that unfetched positions persist for arbitrary values. Copy-source reads are explicitly excluded from this fetched-only formula: subtracting every “used” position would incorrectly remove the payload being copied. Address/count/control use cannot be reconstructed from aggregate counts.

EXPLORATORY subtracting all read positions would predict no free payload for genome20 despite its nine persistent X1 sites. Its p=20 minus six fetched positions also overpredicts the nine sites: five unfetched tail coordinates are not protected by copying. Unfetched status alone is insufficient.

Every non-equal or unaddressable record, additional fetched-site transmission, and offset/minimal-period discrepancy is classified in `cell_exceptions.csv`; family/stage/source aggregates are in `cell_groups.csv`. Generic deficits/excesses remain mechanistically unresolved: aggregate site scores do not identify copying geometry, control use, copy-gate failure or long-term persistence. Missing masks and missing counts are separate from actual deficits/excesses. `cells.csv` covers all listed Z80 mutation, population and serial scan endpoints plus both 6502 final tables. Mutation-table unexecuted counts are joined from the archived trace table; the two partner panels differ, so they are annotations, not identical interventions.

Cheap offspring check: 18372 unique tape/rule combinations executed against two fixed uniform partners; `offspring_periods.csv` gives both actual tapes and periods. This is a sampled output check, not a partner-universal periodicity certificate. It does not change which rows are eligible for the theorem.

Applying the parent's fetched union to a changed offspring is not justified; the offspring's per-site machinery/data-read map is not archived for the full population. Thus the universal *persistent* law cannot be established by these single-generation site scans, even where the count happens to agree.

## EXPLORATORY H3 — contradicted as a universal statement and as lethal-first large transmitters; small-first tendency supported

Z80 first tapes come from the Stage G/I scored world tables. Earliest closed-heritable Z80 cells are all scanned confined cells at the earliest sampled snapshot in each world, not the exact first arrival or a resolved ancestral transition. One Stage G world has no sampled confined cell. 6502 first tapes come from corrected S1 v2 scored outputs, all four arms. Where the first tape is confined and t_rep=t_closed, it is also the earliest scored closed tape; no payload site scan exists for the 6502 first tape. For the single open-first arm C world, the earliest closed tape is recovered from the scorer's chronological insertion-order `judged_tapes` cache (same rule as `score6502.endpoints`), at t_closed. Censored and full-period exceptions are listed in `first_exceptions.csv`.

A world can contribute multiple sampled cells; `first_cells.csv` preserves all exceptions and stages. “Small” here means nontrivial p<L; the full period distributions are retained, rather than choosing an accommodating size cutoff.

EXPLORATORY the earlier scored Stage I first tapes are already confined in 10/10 worlds, all with p=4 or 8 and total scored sites <=4; 0/10 are transmitters by the >=5-site class. Thus “lethal tar first produces large-unit transmitters” is contradicted by these first tapes, even though later earliest population snapshots frequently contain transmitters. The 6502 exception to universally small first tapes is arm B: two detected first tapes have p=L=32; the other two have p=8. Censoring is retained for the remaining 16 B worlds and two D worlds.

## EXPLORATORY H4 — supported for a restricted working-allele set; genome20 outside Proposition 8

All 256 settings were tested at position 0 of ldir32 and position 2 (LD DE low immediate) of the actual genome20_s6003 tape `5e 11 04 c5 ed b8 …`. The latter is an LDDR transmitter with six initial core bytes and 16-bit source wrap, not `XX 5e ed b0`; applying d−4 to it would test the wrong parent. `initial_ring_displacement` is DE mod 2L before copying; for LDDR `effective_d` is the ring displacement after HL first wraps to 0xffff. For its original value 04 these differ: 36 initially, then 20. That discontinuity prevents assuming a constant modulo-ring copy offset.

Every allele has one first encounter per member of a fixed 16-uniform-partner panel. Culture self-copying uses the existing two-generation normalised gain and threshold gen2>=0.3, so a second encounter against a second fixed uniform panel is required; all raw first offspring and periods are preserved. Faithfulness additionally requires >=half offspring be >=75% copies. Inheritance is both original-position and best-shift-aligned byte equality, with changed-output comparison to wild type. Equality alone can be incidental or partner-sourced; the differential flag supports a local causal effect, not a full multigeneration parameter certificate.

- EXPLORATORY ldir32: 99/256 culture-working alleles; 39 faithful; 50 working with >=half aligned allele equality; 11 working satisfying sampled Proposition 8 prerequisites. Working values (hex): 03, 04, 07, 08, 0b, 0c, 13, 14, 15, 1c, 1f, 22, 24, 27, 2b, 2d, 2f, 33, 35, 39, 42, 43, 44, 47, 48, 4b, 4c, 4e, 50, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 5c, 5f, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 66, 67, 68, 6a, 6c, 6d, 6f, 7a, 82, 83, 84, 87, 88, 8b, 8c, 8e, 90, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98, 9c, 9f, a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a6, a7, a8, aa, ac, ad, af, b0, b3, b4, b6, ba, c8, ca, cc, d5, d7, d8, da, dc, dd, df, e3, e8, ea, ec, f3 Eligible d range 4–32; predicted fixed-core payload range 0–28; values and exclusions in `alleles_ldir32.csv`.
- EXPLORATORY genome20_s6003: 15/256 culture-working alleles; 14 faithful; 15 working with >=half aligned allele equality; 0 working satisfying sampled Proposition 8 prerequisites. Working values (hex): 03, 04, 2b, 2c, 53, 54, 55, 7b, 7c, a3, a4, cb, cc, f3, f4 Every Prop 8 payload prediction is missing by design because its forward-prefix conditions fail. `nominal_d_minus_c` is recorded as arithmetic only, not promoted to an inherited payload prediction. The working range must therefore be described by measured offspring periods/allele inheritance, not that proposition.

## EXPLORATORY reproducibility and limits

CPU computed table periods, joins, bounds and summaries. Local GPU commands reuse the assay executor and append observational role bits only; each command has a 58 s alarm and each role dispatch checks elapsed time. No new worlds or large site scans. `execution_*` records source/derived shader hashes and equality-check counts; `allele_execution_*` and offspring rows record executor and runtime. `inputs.csv` hashes the result tables consumed to generate the report. Original archive root `/Users/neo/repos/algocell/experiments/runs` remained read-only; these checks use scored tables and no raw archive writes.

Reproduce from the worktree `experiments` directory with `/Users/neo/repos/algocell/experiments/.venv/bin/python crystal_check.py tables`; then `probe --key KEY` for the five X1 keys, `alleles --key KEY` for ldir32/genome20_s6003, `offset-examples`, and `offspring --source classes --L L --stage STAGE` per observed stage/length, or `offspring --source 6502 --L L --stage ARM`. Finish with `report`. Report-only generation requires no GPU.
